prompt: How do I get dog hair out of my car seats?
engine: ChatGPT (chatgpt.com, logged out, site data cleared before the prompt)
answer:
Dog hair can be ridiculously hard to get out of car seats, especially when it gets woven into the fabric. The trick is to loosen the hair first, then vacuum it up rather than just vacuuming over it.

5 best ways to remove dog hair from car seats
 

1. Rubber brush or pet hair removal tool 
Best
overall

Use short, firm strokes in one direction to pull embedded hair into clumps. A rubber upholstery brush is especially effective on cloth seats.

Best for: Heavy, stubborn buildup.

 

2. Damp rubber glove

Put on a rubber dishwashing glove, lightly dampen it, and rub the seat in one direction. The hair should gather into little balls you can pick up.

Best for: A cheap, easy DIY solution.

 

3. Silicone squeegee

Drag it firmly across the seat in short strokes. It grips hair and pulls it out of the fabric.

Best for: Large areas and thick layers of fur.

 

4. Vacuum with a brush attachment

Vacuum after loosening the hair with a rubber tool. Use a crevice attachment along seat seams and between the cushions.

Best for: Picking up loose hair and finishing the job.

 

5. Pet hair stone

Gently sweep a purpose-made upholstery hair-removal stone across the fabric to lift deeply embedded fur.

Best for: Very stubborn hair on durable cloth upholstery. Test an inconspicuous spot first; it can snag or damage delicate fabric.

The quickest method I'd recommend

Remove any loose items and vacuum the seats.

Use a rubber brush or damp rubber glove to pull embedded fur into clumps.

Vacuum the clumps up.

Use a crevice tool around seams and seat edges.

Repeat on the stubborn patches.

Tip: Avoid soaking the seats. Too much water can push hair deeper into the fabric and make cleanup harder.
